value.body: A B.Com with a focus on cross-border trade — run as B.Com (International Business) or B.Com (Foreign Trade) at some universities, and as a set of electives at others. On top of the commerce core, you study the international business environment, export-import procedures and documentation, foreign exchange, international marketing, trade finance, and trade policy and agreements.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Class 12 (commerce preferred, not always required). Central and many other universities admit through CUET-UG; others admit on Class 12 marks or their own process. Where International Business is a named programme, you choose it at admission; elsewhere you pick trade and international-business electives in later semesters.

value.title: At a glance
items: Entry work is mostly documentation and coordination — at exporters and importers, freight forwarders, customs brokers and bank trade-finance desks.
Familiarity with Incoterms and shipping documents (invoice, packing list, shipping bill, bill of lading, letter of credit) is commonly expected.
A foreign language helps for some buyer-facing roles but is rarely required.
Common next steps: an MBA (International Business), an M.Com, or a master's abroad.
